deep.reconstruction:
Context. Sections III–V of this bundle state one scheme: collect points ϖ on an edge of a small square in the (ξ,η)-plane. At each point where a transformed coordinate is an integer, attach a sign ε = ±1. The linear relations on this page and on f.22 (V) are solved exactly by two Gaussian-integer multiplications (my reconstruction, checked against every line):
  X + iY = (A + iB)(ξ + iη), i.e. X = Aξ − Bη, Y = Bξ + Aη;
  x + iy = (a + ib)(ξ + iη), i.e. x = aξ − bη, y = bξ + aη.
The abbreviations are forced (my identification):
  D = A² + B², the norm of M = A + iB;
  α = aA + bB;
  ℭ = Ab − aB.
The two products give
  x + iy = (a+ib)(X+iY)/(A+iB) = [α X + ℭ Y + i(α Y − ℭ X)]/D, using (a+ib)(A−iB) = α + iℭ.

Section IV. Collect all ϖ such that:
  - ξ = ½ + ½ω. I read ω as an infinitesimal positive displacement, so the edge is ξ = ½ pushed slightly to the right. This is my interpretation; it removes the boundary cases in the floor functions.
  - 0 < η < ½. The word 'grösser' is struck out.
  - X or Y is an integer.
Set ε = sign of Im( iM/(P − P⁰) ), which equals sign of Re( M/(P − P⁰) ). P, P⁰ are presumably the image point and a reference point in the M-picture. Section V is the same with m, p, p°.

First class (X integer). Using 2ξ = 1 + ω, η = (Aξ − X)/B, so 2Bη = A − 2X + Aω. Substituting:
  x = aξ − bη = ((aB − bA)ξ + bX)/B, so 2Bx = −ℭ + 2bX − ℭω;
  y = bξ + aη = ((aA + bB)ξ − aX)/B, so 2By = α − 2aX + αω;
  Y = Bξ + Aη = ((A² + B²)ξ − AX)/B, so 2BY = D − 2AX + Dω.
Sign rule. The bracket [Y] is Gauss's integer-part bracket; Y itself is not an integer here. The three conditions are: B > 0, X even, [Y] even. ε = +1 if one or three of them hold, −1 if none or two. Compactly, ε = sgn(B)·(−1)^(X + [Y]).

Second class (Y integer). η = (Y − Bξ)/A, so 2Aη = −B + 2Y − Bω. Then:
  x = ((aA + bB)ξ − bY)/A, so 2Ax = α − 2bY + αω;
  y = ((bA − aB)ξ + aY)/A, so 2Ay = ℭ + 2aY + ℭω;
  X = ((A² + B²)ξ − BY)/A, so 2AX = D − 2BY + Dω.
Sign rule: ε = +1 if an odd number of {A > 0, [X] even, Y even} hold, else −1. That is ε = sgn(A)·(−1)^([X] + Y).

Purpose (my interpretation). This is a signed count of the crossings of the image of the edge ξ = ½, 0 < η < ½ of the quarter square 0 < ξ, η < ½ with the integer grid lines, under multiplication by M = A + iB (here) or m = a + ib (in V). Section III does another part of the boundary. The quarter square is the natural 'half system' of residues for Gaussian integers, as in a Gauss-lemma-type evaluation of the biquadratic character. Carrying x, y alongside X, Y suggests a simultaneous two-modulus comparison of the reciprocity type. The parity factors (−1)^(X + [Y]) are exactly the kind of quantities that arise in such lattice-point counts.
errors: No mathematical errors once the blots are read correctly.
In 2Bx the operator before ℭω is blotted; the algebra requires −ℭω, since −ℭ(1+ω) comes from 2ξ = 1+ω.
In 2Aη the operator before Bω is blotted; the algebra requires −Bω. The analogous unclear sign on f.22 (2aη = −b + 2y ? bω) must likewise be −.

The sign rules are stated loosely ('B positiv, X, [Y] gerade oder bei einer Bedingung'). Read as 'all three or exactly one of the three conditions', they give the consistent closed form ε = sgn(B)(−1)^(X+[Y]). The second-class rule originally began 'oder wenn', which was struck out.
The coefficient of X in 2BY is the ordinary A (= Re M), not a separate Gothic quantity; any reading of it as Gothic 𝔄 must denote A.

results.what: Parametrization of the crossings of the segment ξ = ½+0, 0<η<½ with integer grid lines under z ↦ (A+iB)z, with simultaneous coordinates of the same point under z ↦ (a+ib)z, via α = aA+bB, ℭ = Ab−aB, D = A²+B²
results.modern_name: Lattice-point / grid-line crossing count for Gaussian integers (geometric Gauss-lemma style evaluation of a quartic character)
results.usually_credited_to: Geometric lattice-counting proofs of reciprocity: Eisenstein (1844) for the quadratic case; Gauss-lemma analogues for biquadratic residues by Eisenstein, Busche and others later in the 19th c.

results.what: Sign/parity rule ε = sgn(B)(−1)^(X+[Y]) (resp. sgn(A)(−1)^([X]+Y)) for the orientation of each crossing
results.modern_name: Orientation/parity bookkeeping in a winding-number or lattice-point count

results.usually_credited_to: Gauss (bracket notation, 1808 third proof of quadratic reciprocity)

deep.surprise_reason: These are elementary linear-algebra special rules, internally consistent, for a signed boundary-crossing count tied to Gaussian-integer multiplication on a quarter square. It plausibly belongs to Gauss's unpublished work toward biquadratic reciprocity, which is known to exist in general. If it were shown to be a complete geometric lattice-crossing proof, that would be notable. The page alone shows only bookkeeping, so the surprise is modest.

checkable.sympy: A,B,a,b,X,w=symbols('A B a b X w'); xi=(1+w)/2; eta=(A*xi-X)/B; simplify(2*B*eta-(A-2*X+A*w))
checkable.asserts: First class η-formula follows from X = Aξ − Bη with ξ = (1+ω)/2 (result 0)

checkable.sympy: A,B,a,b,X,w=symbols('A B a b X w'); xi=(1+w)/2; eta=(A*xi-X)/B; C=A*b-a*B; simplify(2*B*(a*xi-b*eta)-(-C+2*b*X-C*w))
checkable.asserts: 2Bx = −ℭ + 2bX − ℭω with ℭ = Ab − aB (result 0; the blotted sign is minus)

checkable.sympy: A,B,a,b,X,w=symbols('A B a b X w'); xi=(1+w)/2; eta=(A*xi-X)/B; al=a*A+b*B; simplify(2*B*(b*xi+a*eta)-(al-2*a*X+al*w))
checkable.asserts: 2By = α − 2aX + αω with α = aA + bB

checkable.sympy: A,B,X,w=symbols('A B X w'); xi=(1+w)/2; eta=(A*xi-X)/B; D=A**2+B**2; simplify(2*B*(B*xi+A*eta)-(D-2*A*X+D*w))
checkable.asserts: 2BY = D − 2AX + Dω with D = A² + B²

checkable.sympy: A,B,Y,w=symbols('A B Y w'); xi=(1+w)/2; eta=(Y-B*xi)/A; simplify(2*A*eta-(-B+2*Y-B*w))
checkable.asserts: Second class η-formula from Y = Bξ + Aη (blotted sign is minus)

checkable.sympy: A,B,a,b,Y,w=symbols('A B a b Y w'); xi=(1+w)/2; eta=(Y-B*xi)/A; al=a*A+b*B; C=A*b-a*B; [simplify(2*A*(a*xi-b*eta)-(al-2*b*Y+al*w)), simplify(2*A*(b*xi+a*eta)-(C+2*a*Y+C*w))]
A,B,Y,w=symbols('A B Y w'); xi=(1+w)/2; eta=(Y-B*xi)/A; D=A**2+B**2; simplify(2*A*(A*xi-B*eta)-(D-2*B*Y+D*w))
A,B,a,b,xi,eta=symbols('A B a b xi eta',real=True); al=a*A+b*B; C=A*b-a*B; D=A**2+B**2; X=A*xi-B*eta; Y=B*xi+A*eta; simplify(expand((a*xi-b*eta)+I*(b*xi+a*eta) - ((al*X+C*Y)+I*(al*Y-C*X))/D))
checkable.asserts: x+iy = (a+ib)(X+iY)/(A+iB) expressed through α, ℭ, D (result 0)

transcription_corrections: Line 2: read ξ = ½ + ½ω (not ½ + (i/2)ω). The formulas require 2ξ = 1 + ω.
2Bx = −ℭ + 2bX − ℭω: the blotted operator is a minus.
2Aη = −B + 2Y − Bω: the blotted operator is a minus, not plus.
2BY = D − 2AX + Dω: the coefficient is the ordinary A, not a Gothic 𝔄.
'[Y]' and '[X]' are Gauss's integer-part brackets as written in the manuscript, not editorial insertions.
First sign rule: 'bei einer Bedingung'; the second line reads 'bei keiner oder zwei Bedingungen' (with 'beir' corrected).
